narrative: Material PL1__M63E0EC4 exhibits smooth, high-volume demand averaging 630 units/day with a CV of 0.31, indicating stable and predictable consumption. Lead times average 4.3 working days but show moderate variability (CV=0.33), which is the dominant driver of safety stock requirements. Two extreme lead-time data points (>9,000 days) were identified as data errors and excluded. The recommended (r,Q) policy with SS=1,813 and OQ=3,044 achieves the 95% service level target while respecting the 4,857-unit storage capacity — a binding constraint that leaves zero headroom for safety stock increases without additional storage.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth, non-intermittent demand (CV=0.31, 100% non-zero) with moderate lead time variability makes the classic (r,Q) continuous review policy optimal. EOQ minimises ordering-vs-holding cost trade-off; the reorder point incorporates safety stock calibrated to the 95th percentile of lead-time demand distribution. No intermittency correction (Croston/SBA) required.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity is exactly binding at the recommended policy (SS+OQ=4857 = max_storage_units). If lead time variability increases or demand spikes, safety stock cannot be increased without breaching storage limits. Recommend negotiating a 5-10% storage buffer or implementing vendor-managed inventory to reduce the safety stock burden.
